---
title: "matrix() fills column by column"
ref: IDX-06
categories: [Indexing]
impact: incoherent
extrait: 'matrix(1:6, nrow = 2)[1, ]'
reponse: '1 3 5'
attendu: "`1 2 3`, the first row filled reading from left to right"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
m <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2)
m
m[1, ]
```
:::

## Why

R stores a matrix as a single vector, column after column. `matrix()` therefore fills the first column first, then the second. That is the opposite of reading order, and of the way you often copy a table typed in row by row.

The same order applies the other way round: `as.vector(m)` reads the values back column by column.

## The fix

Set `byrow = TRUE` when the values are given row by row.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
m <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
m
m[1, ]
```
:::
